name: Detect n8n workflows that succeed with zero output using the n8n API, Data Tables and Slack

nodes.name: Did The Sweep Have Blind Spots?
Report The Blind Spots To Slack
Treat A Never-Run Workflow As Dark
Note The n8n API Read Failed

parameters.content:
## Catch the workflows that succeed and produce nothing

Most n8n monitoring watches for failures. An execution errors, the error trigger fires, somebody goes and fixes it. The run nobody catches is the other one: the schedule fires on time, every node goes green, and zero rows come out the far end. Nothing in n8n treats that as a problem, so the executions list fills up with ticks while the data quietly goes stale.

I built this after one of my own scheduled jobs spent weeks reporting success and writing nothing. No error ever fired, because nothing had errored. So this workflow reads the item counts inside your own executions and treats an empty successful run as a fault in its own right.

**Who's it for**

Anyone running scheduled n8n workflows they cannot eyeball every morning. If you run a nightly sync or a scheduled scraper, an empty run and a good run look identical from the outside.

**How it works**

A Data Table holds one row per workflow you watch, carrying how often it should run and how many items a healthy run produces. Every hour the watchdog reads that list, asks the n8n API for each workflow's last successful execution, then opens that execution's run data and counts the items its final node actually returned. Each workflow lands in one of four states: HEALTHY, EMPTY for green but produced nothing, STALE for nothing succeeded inside the expected window, and DARK for nothing succeeded in a long time. The verdict is written back to the table, and Slack only hears about it when the state changes or the same fault survives the cooldown. At the end the watchdog reads the table back and names any row it could not check, so a blind spot arrives as a blind spot instead of a silent pass.

**How to set up**

1. Create a Data Table called workflow_output_watchdog with these columns: workflow_id (string), label (string), expect_every_minutes (number), min_items (number), last_state (string), consecutive_misses (number), last_checked_at (string), last_healthy_at (string), last_alert_at (string), last_produced_items (number), last_execution_id (string).
2. Add one row per workflow you want watched. Set expect_every_minutes to its schedule and min_items to the smallest number of items a healthy run returns.
3. Point both Data Table nodes at your table, then connect your n8n API credential and your Slack credential.
4. Open Watchdog Settings and set your instance URL so every alert carries a clickable link to the execution behind it.

**Requirements**

An n8n API credential and a Slack credential. Data Tables need to be available on your instance.

**How to customize**

graceMultiplier decides how far past its schedule a workflow drifts before it counts as stale. alertCooldownMinutes and escalateAfterMisses control how loud a repeat fault gets. Swap the Slack nodes for Gmail, Telegram or a plain webhook without touching the logic. If a workflow legitimately returns nothing most of the time, set its min_items to 0 and it gets judged on freshness alone.

---

Built by **Fractional HQ** · https://fractionalhq.uk

**Need help customising this, or want the whole thing built and handed over working?** I build automation systems for small teams. Get in touch: https://fractionalhq.uk/brief

## 1. Configure it in one place

One row per watched workflow lives in the Data Table. Watchdog Settings holds the thresholds, so changing how tolerant the watchdog is never means editing logic.

## 2. Read what the run actually produced

The first call finds the last successful execution. The second opens that execution and counts the items its final node returned. If either call fails I mark the row unreadable, rather than quietly skipping it and calling the sweep complete.

## 3. Decide, then remember

Four states, written back to the same row. The stored state is what lets the next sweep tell a brand new fault from one that has been sitting there since Tuesday.

## 4. Alert only when it earns it

A state change goes to Slack immediately. A fault that persists waits out the cooldown, and anything past escalateAfterMisses arrives marked as escalated.

## 5. Report the watchdog's own blind spots

The ledger gets read back after the sweep. Any row that was not checked this run is named in the report, because I would rather see a gap than trust a monitor that hides its own.
